<STRUCT_0001>
In the following few sections we will use the following notions:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> A sheaf of ideals <MATH_0001> on
a ringed space <MATH_0002> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>locally nilpotent<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
if any local section of <MATH_0003> is locally nilpotent.
Compare with Algebra, Item <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0004> A <TEXTITOPEN_0002>thickening<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> of ringed spaces is a morphism
<MATH_0004> of ringed spaces
such that
<STRUCT_0005>
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0005> induces a homeomorphism <MATH_0006>,
<STRUCT_0007> the map <MATH_0007>
is surjective, and
<STRUCT_0008> the kernel of <MATH_0008> is a locally nilpotent sheaf of ideals.
<STRUCT_0009>
<STRUCT_0010> A <TEXTITOPEN_0003>first order thickening<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> of ringed spaces is a thickening
<MATH_0009> of ringed spaces
such that <MATH_0010> has square zero.
<STRUCT_0011> It is clear how to define <TEXTITOPEN_0004>morphisms of thickenings<TEXTITCLOSE_0004>,
<TEXTITOPEN_0005>morphisms of thickenings over a base ringed space<TEXTITCLOSE_0005>, etc.
<STRUCT_0012>
If <MATH_0011> is a thickening
of ringed spaces then we identify the underlying topological spaces
and think of <MATH_0012>, <MATH_0013>, and
<MATH_0014> as sheaves on <MATH_0015>. We obtain
a short exact sequence
<MATH_0016>
of <MATH_0017>-modules. By
Modules, Lemma <REF_0002>
the category of <MATH_0018>-modules is equivalent to the category
of <MATH_0019>-modules annihilated by <MATH_0020>. In particular,
if <MATH_0021> is a first order thickening, then
<MATH_0022> is a <MATH_0023>-module.
